analysis.title: What to watch in the week ahead
key_insights: Tech sold off sharply on Friday as investors questioned whether AI revenues can justify the scale and financing of infrastructure spend. Nasdaq 100 fell 5.6% and S&P 500 fell 3.7% on the day.

Nasdaq 100 ended the week 19.8% below its October high, near bear market territory. S&P 500 is 11.5% below its high, in correction territory. VIX rose to nearly 36, the highest since the spring 2025 tariff turmoil.
UBS estimates US tech will have invested nearly USD 5tr in AI infrastructure by end-2028. AI model and application revenues may need to reach at least USD 1.5tr by 2030 for an adequate return.

UBS expects elevated volatility near term but says the economic expansion, earnings cycle and structural AI investment case are not broken. Base case of robust earnings and resilient growth is consistent with further equity gains in 2027.
Global equities were recently downgraded from Attractive to Neutral on elevated expectations, high index concentration and a wider range of AI outcomes.
Equity advice is to reduce concentration and rebalance toward strategic targets, building positions gradually. Preferred region is the Eurozone, preferred sectors are industrials and health care.
Within tech, UBS prefers financially strong hyperscalers with tangible monetization and select leaders in compute, foundry, semiconductor equipment and infrastructure software.
October Fed minutes showed almost all officials thought further hikes would be needed. Markets price a near certainty of a 25bp hike in December, with more tightening expected in Q1.
Treasuries rallied despite hawkish minutes. The 10-year yield fell 19bp to 4.95% and the 2-year fell nearly 20bp, its strongest weekly performance since August 2025.

This week's US data (core PCE, Q3 GDP second estimate, income and spending, durables, confidence, housing) will test gradual tightening. Persistent inflation with resilient demand raises the risk of consecutive hikes.
UBS expects 25bp Fed hikes in December and March 2027, and sees US inflation falling to 2.3% in 2027 from 3.4% in 2026.
Fixed income is rated Attractive with a preference for intermediate duration of 2 to 10 years. Best returns are seen in EM and high yield bonds.

Year Ahead 2027 base case is constructive: trend growth, rising earnings, rising AI investment, later inflation moderation. Resilience via diversification into bonds, commodities, currencies and alternatives is advised.

Chart of the week suggests capital preservation for concentrated holders and structured yield strategies to monetize elevated option premiums, sized and diversified. Staggered maturities and pre-defined entry levels help build exposure.
